question.problem:
Find the solutions of $78x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,406).$ Express your answers as nonnegative integers smaller than $406,$ and in ascending order. 

*Hint: You may use the fact that $\text{gcd}(78,406)=2.$*

${x}_{1}≡$
{{field-1}}
$,\,{x}_{2}≡$
{{field-2}}
$\,(\text{mod}\,406)$
question.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=78$ and $n=406$, and we're given that

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(78,406)=2.
$$

Since $b=4$ is divisible by $2,$ our congruence has $2$ solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}78x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,406) \\ 2\cdot 39x & ≡2\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,2\cdot 203) \\ \cancel{2}\cdot 39x & ≡\cancel{2}\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{2}\cdot 203) \\ 39x & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,203)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in this new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=39$ and ${n}_{1}=203$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(39,203)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $203.$

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $39\,(\text{mod}\,203).$ To find the inverse of $39\,(\text{mod}\,203),$ we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}203 & = & 39\cdot 5 & + & 8\, & ⇔ & \,8 & = & 203-39\cdot 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 39 & = & 8\cdot 4 & + & 7\, & ⇔ & \,7 & = & 39-8\cdot 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 8 & = & 7\cdot 1 & + & 1\, & ⇔ & \,1 & = & 8-7\cdot 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 7 & = & 7\cdot 1 & + & 0\, &  & \, &  & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

$$
1=5\cdot 203-26\cdot 39
$$

We can write this result in modulo $203,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}5\cdot 203-26\cdot 39 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ -26\cdot 39 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ (203-26)\cdot 39 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ 177\cdot 39 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,203)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse of $39$ modulo $203$ is $177.$

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $177,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}39x & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ 177\cdot 39x & ≡177\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ x & ≡354 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ x & ≡203+151 &  & (\text{mod}\,203) \\ x & ≡151 &  & (\text{mod}\,203)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡151\,(\text{mod}\,203).$

But our original congruence was modulo $406$ (not modulo $203$). To find all the solutions modulo $406,$ we repeatedly add $203$ to $151$ modulo $406$ until we reach the number $151$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡151 &  & (\text{mod}\,406) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡151+203≡354 &  & (\text{mod}\,406) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡354+203≡557≡406+151≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,406)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2}≡151,\,354,\,(\text{mod}\,406).
$$
